clue.text: Piece of furniture having unpleasant smell? Fine when in church

parts.note: BO is body odour
OK means fine, all right

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
as can mean when (as I left = when I left)

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a smelly item of furniture that would be fine if kept in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of shelves for storing volumes is a familiar household furnishing.

clue.text: Somewhere off the beaten track, young person starts to visit Roman city

indicators.note: to visit means going inside, so these letters enter the city

parts.note: Bath in England was the Roman city of Aquae Sulis

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of young and person

explanation.surface: A young traveller sets off for a Roman city by a little-used road.
explanation.definitionFit: A side lane or secluded route lies away from the main roads.

clue.text: Writer of ordinary book's nothing to Lorraine

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
rien is French for nothing, and Lorraine is a region of France

explanation.surface: An everyday book from some writer means nothing to a woman named Lorraine.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorraine looks like a woman's name; it is the French region, asking for the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna and Flann, two Irish novelists, share this surname, fitting the Irish theme.

clue.text: The best thing that goes with strawberries

definitions.meaning: the pick of the bunch, the finest part
the traditional partner of strawberries, as at Wimbledon

explanation.surface: Praise for the ideal companion to strawberries.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the elite and the dairy topping eaten with summer strawberries.

clue.text: Johnson's occasionally in blue during visit

indicators.note: during means one piece is set within the other

parts.note: a stay is a visit

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter of in blue

explanation.surface: Johnson sometimes feels down while away on a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like Boris Johnson; Stanley is his father, a former MEP and writer. The 's is read as is.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Johnson, father of the former Prime Minister, is a Johnson by surname.

clue.text: Hot priest shows wit

indicators.note: hot can mean agitated or fiery, signalling that the letters of priest are stirred up

explanation.surface: An attractive clergyman proves to be clever and funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is French-borrowed liveliness of mind, a synonym for quick humour.

clue.text: People wasting money stop eating chips? On the contrary

indicators.note: eating means one piece swallows another
On the contrary means the eating happens the other way round to what is written: the chips eat the stop

parts.note: spalls are chips or splinters of stone
end means stop

explanation.surface: Spendthrifts are told to stop eating chips, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Spendthrifts or wastrels who fritter away all their cash.

clue.text: Suddenly moved back from playground that's greasy

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public playground
oiled means greasy

explanation.surface: Someone jumped back from a grimy children's play area.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch or spring back in shock or disgust, as a gun kicks back.

clue.text: They keep records of unbelievable husband leaving Maidenhead

parts.note: a tall story is an unbelievable one

indicators.note: leaving means the letter departs from the word

parts.note: maidenhead is an old word for the hymen, and also a town in Berkshire

explanation.surface: An incredible tale of a husband walking out of Maidenhead, a town west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerks who count and record goods or payments, keeping tallies.

clue.text: Normal People full of sex appeal? That's cheesy!

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: the thing that is cheese

parts.note: par is the normal standard, as in feeling below par

indicators.note: full of means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: A comment on Sally Rooney's novel Normal People, mocking its sexy content as cheesy.
explanation.walkthrough: Normal People is Sally Rooney's novel, the puzzle's theme; the title is split into two pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian hard grated variety is a cheese, so it is something cheesy.

clue.text: Case of Marianne disrupting class, abandoning school — some spirit!

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters
disrupting suggests throwing the remaining letters of class into disorder
abandoning means a letter is dropped from class

explanation.surface: Marianne, a character in Normal People, causes trouble in class and skips school, showing real spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: ME (the outside of Marianne) comes first; CLAS (class abandoning one S) is then disrupted into SCAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexican agave liquor is one example of a distilled spirit.

clue.text: Time together to become less intense, they say

indicators.note: they say means the clue word is heard spoken, so a sound-alike is needed

parts.note: to sink is to decline or diminish

explanation.surface: A remark that shared time fades over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for synchronisation, being simultaneous, matched in timing.

clue.text: In relation to 'heat': time woman's getting male partner

parts.note: her stands for a woman; the 's is read as is
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Talk of heat as a woman finds herself a boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes things done with respect to warmth or temperature.

clue.text: Flower girl found at Platform 25

definitions.note: a girl's name that is also a flower

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform
Y is the 25th letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A bridesmaid with flowers spotted at a railway platform numbered 25.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 25 looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but here it is just the alphabet's 25th letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The common lawn bloom with white petals also serves as a girl's first name.

clue.text: Connell regularly meets Peggy, at last alone

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of Connell
at last means take the final letter of Peggy

explanation.surface: Connell, from Normal People, keeps meeting Peggy, but ends up by himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adverbially, both words mean solely, with nobody or nothing else.

clue.text: Deranged Etonian securing university grant without bombast? Sweet!

indicators.note: securing means holding something tight inside
deranged means jumbled, so the letters of Etonian are mixed
without means the letters are removed

parts.note: a rant is bombast, overblown talk

explanation.surface: A deranged Old Etonian secures a student grant with no ranting, and is pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: Etonian is mixed to NOATINE, which holds U plus G (grant losing RANT).
explanation.definitionFit: A confection of nougat with nuts, a type of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Porter perhaps keeps on offering student accommodation?

indicators.note: keeps means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: Cole Porter, the songwriter, is a Porter
on and leg are both names for the same side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A building porter looks after something students might live in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a college porter; the porter is in fact the composer Cole Porter. Trinity College Dublin is where much of Normal People is set.
explanation.definitionFit: A university hall or institution where undergraduates may live, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Playwright's woman managed to steal papers

parts.note: she stands for a woman

indicators.note: to steal means taking something in, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: ran means managed
ID, identity documents, are papers

explanation.surface: A dramatist's female associate manages to steal some documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote The School for Scandal and The Rivals.

clue.text: Friendly guy supporting Jamie after dropping clothes

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means placed underneath
after dropping clothes means the outer letters of Jamie are removed

parts.note: a guy is a supporting rope, as a cable is

explanation.surface: A sociable chap backs Jamie, who has stripped off.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means agreeable and well-disposed, as in an amicable divorce.

clue.text: Meat: food rejected in German city

parts.note: ham is a meat

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: grub is informal for food

explanation.surface: A meal is turned away in a German city, perhaps by a fussy diner.
explanation.definitionFit: The large port on the Elbe is Germany's second-largest city.

clue.text: Musical performance on island

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above

parts.note: a gig is a performance by musicians

explanation.surface: A musical show staged on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lerner and Loewe stage and film show of 1958 is a musical.

clue.text: It's nonsense to be quiet

parts.note: sh is the sound used to ask for silence

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses keeping silent as pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for rubbish or claptrap.

clue.text: Taking part in attempt to create threesome

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to be in it is to be taking part

explanation.surface: Joining an attempt to form a group of three.
explanation.walkthrough: Trinity College Dublin is where Connell and Marianne study in Normal People.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinity is a group of three, most famously the Christian Godhead.

clue.text: Louis XIV discovered Germany's cruel

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, its first and last letters stripped away

parts.note: the French king Louis XIV was known as the Sun King
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: History finds the French king's Germany policy harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkind means harsh or uncaring, a milder synonym for cruel.

clue.text: Footballer, one given welcome by coach Hodgson

indicators.note: given welcome by means being taken in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Roy Hodgson is a former England football manager

explanation.surface: A player welcomed by the England manager Roy Hodgson.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally Rooney, the author of Normal People, shares the name with Wayne, the England striker.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayne, England's former record goal scorer, played for Manchester United.

clue.text: Correct answer will reveal body parts

indicators.note: will reveal means the letters are sitting inside the words Correct answer

explanation.surface: The right solution will expose some anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of rectum, the final section of the large intestine, so organs of the body.

clue.text: 26 unhappy about smooth melodic effect

indicators.note: about means one piece wraps around the other
unhappy suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: 26 refers to the answer to 26 down, the Irish county
to sand is to smooth

explanation.surface: An Irish county, unhappy about a smooth musical slide.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram GLISO of the 26 answer wraps around SAND. Sligo is the Irish county where Normal People begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid slide up or down a scale is a musical ornament played for effect.

clue.text: County should look into golden opportunities for starters

indicators.note: for starters means take the first letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: Advice that a county ought to explore its promising chances.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish shire in Connacht on the north-west coast is a county of Ireland.

clue.text: Here in Ireland, couple's without love (largely what love is, they say)

indicators.note: without means one letter is taken away

parts.note: a couple is a duo
love is zero in tennis, hence O

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: the saying goes that love is blind

explanation.surface: A pair, out of love, reflects on the proverb about love's blindness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish capital is a place in Ireland, and the 'here' is where the characters of the theme go to study.

clue.text: Split vote in Parliament

definitions.meaning: a split or separation into parts
MPs voting by walking into lobbies is a formal count in the Commons

explanation.surface: A parliamentary vote that divides opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a separation and the formal counted vote in the House of Commons.

clue.text: Required: E, N and D, sorted in various quantities

parts.words: E, N and D, sorted in various quantities
parts.note: the three letters, used one, two or three times each and rearranged, spell the word

explanation.surface: An instruction from a puzzle about rearranging letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer has one N, three Es and two Ds: the given letters, sorted, in differing amounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that was required was wanted or necessary, the past participle of a verb meaning to want.

clue.text: I listened to fado performance, end of July, in the sun

indicators.note: listened means the word is heard rather than read, so take its sound

parts.note: the pronoun I, said aloud

indicators.note: a performance of the letters puts them into a new order
end of means the final letter of July

explanation.surface: Someone listened to Portuguese fado sung out in the sunshine at the close of July.
explanation.walkthrough: The pronoun I sounds like EYE; FADO rearranged gives OFDA, then Y ends July.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic phrase for the sun, the eye that watches the daytime sky.
